newsitem.title: USA: TCF sees no branch closings due to deal.
newsitem.headline: TCF sees no branch closings due to deal.

text.p: TCF Financial Corp said Monday it does not expect to close any bank branches due to its proposed merger with Standard Financial Inc.
Earlier, TCF said it agreed to a $424 million merger with Standard Financial. Standard shares are valued at about $25 each in the deal.

"This union significantly expands our profitable and growing Illinois franchise," William Cooper, TCF Chairman, said in a statement. "Chicago has long been an attractive market for TCF...and Standard has an exemplary tradition of meeting community banking needs."
After the merger, Standard's bank branches will be combined with TCF Bank Illinois. The directors of Standard will join TCF Bank Illinois' board of directors.
David Mackiewich, chairman and president of Standard Financial, will become executive chairman of TCF Bank Illinois and a director of TCF Financial.
Michael Johnstone, president and chief execuuctive officer of TCF Bank Illinois, will continue in that capacity.
Standard, a thrift institution, has $2.4 billion in assets and 14 full-service offices on the southwest side of Chicago and in the nearby southwestern and western suburbs.
TCF is a stock savings bank holding company with $7.1 billion in assets and more than 260 financial services offices.

"Joining TCF will accelerate our transformation to a leading consumer bank, for the benefit of our shareholders, customers, and the communities we serve," Mackiewich said in a statement. "We will have access to a broader range of products and services, convenient banking locations -- including seven-day banking at supermarkets and 248 cash station ATMs (automatic teller machines) -- and the financial resources of a dynamic regional bank."
